sections.title: How does the Save percentage calculator work?
sections.html:
The Save percentage calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports goalkeeper save percentage in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the goalkeeper saves, the shots against the goalkeeper, the total shots on target and the total save index.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Save percentage calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Goalkeeper save percentage=goalkeeper saves ÷ shots against the goalkeeper
Goalkeeper save percentage=goalkeeper save index
Total saves=total save percentage × total shots on target
Total save percentage=total save index
Goals allowed=GAA × minutes played ÷ regulation time in minutes

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Goalkeeper saves = 10 and Shots against the goalkeeper = 10. Working through the relationship above gives Goalkeeper save percentage = 100 % and Goalkeeper save index = 1.

Read it as a template. Every number above can be replaced with one of yours; only the relationship between them is fixed.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Goalkeeper save percentage = 100 % and Goalkeeper save index = 1 should be roughly the size you expected from Goalkeeper saves = 10 and Shots against the goalkeeper = 10.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • %, opening in percent

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Save percentage calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Planning a session around a target you already know
  • Comparing two athletes or two attempts fairly
  • Tracking progress across a training block
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the goalkeeper saves, the shots against the goalkeeper and the total shots on target — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Save percentage calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns goalkeeper save percentage, derived from the goalkeeper saves, the shots against the goalkeeper and the total shots on target. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Save percentage calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the goalkeeper saves, the shots against the goalkeeper, the total shots on target and the total save index, which is 7 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter goalkeeper save percentage in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Goalkeeper save percentage opens in percent and the chip beside it offers 6 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Goalkeeper save percentage = 100 %. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Save percentage calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
